_metadata.description: Lifetime value benchmarks by brand tier for automotive dealerships
sources: NADA Data Annual Financial Profile (2024 edition)
J.D. Power U.S. Service Retention Study 2024
_metadata.notes: Values are industry averages. Individual dealer performance varies. GM/GSM should validate against their own DMS data.

luxury.label: Luxury (BMW, Mercedes, Audi, Lexus, Porsche, Land Rover, Volvo, Genesis, Acura, INFINITI, Cadillac, Lincoln)
luxury.notes: Higher front gross and service retention offset higher acquisition costs. Luxury shoppers research more online, so VDP engagement metrics are critical.

mainstream_import.label: Mainstream Import (Toyota, Honda, Nissan, Hyundai, Kia, Mazda, Subaru, VW, Mitsubishi)
mainstream_import.notes: Volume-driven. CPL efficiency matters more here than luxury tier. High service retention for Toyota/Honda skews tier average up.

domestic_truck_suv.label: Domestic Truck/SUV-Heavy (Ford, Chevrolet, RAM, GMC, Jeep)
domestic_truck_suv.notes: Strong F&I income on trucks. Lower service retention than imports. Conquest campaigns against other domestic brands can be cost-effective.

domestic_car.label: Domestic Car-Heavy (Chrysler, Dodge, Buick)
domestic_car.notes: Lower LTV means tighter CAC tolerance. Spend efficiency is paramount. Dodge has some truck/SUV overlap via Durango and Hornet.
